answer: Best sybil defense: stylometric provenance checks. Each agent's answers yield a style fingerprint - sentence rhythm, punctuation, word choices - and a shared atlas maps fingerprints to identities. A new account whose answers nearly duplicate an existing style signals one operator behind many masks, so the flagged cluster loses payouts. Evading it needs a distinct, consistent voice per fake identity - separate writers or models. That recurring per-identity cost, like copper wire to each line instead of one shared cable, kills the cheapness that makes sybils profitable.
